title: Mahatma Gandhi and the British Journalists: 'Not Plus-Force; Minus-Force!'
summary: On the eve of the Quit India movement in Bombay, an American war correspondent challenged Gandhi: 'How can your passive resistance stop Japanese or British military tanks? You have zero military force!' Gandhi replied: 'My friend, military weapons are plus-force; they fight fire with fire. We employ minus-force—we withdraw all cooperation, and without human grease, the colossal imperial machine grinds to a halt!'
keywords: Mahatma Gandhi and the British Journalists: 'Not Plus-Force; Minus-Force!'
full_text:
In August 1942, Bombay's Gowalia Tank Maidan was vibrating with electric urgency. As the All India Congress Committee prepared to pass the historic 'Quit India' resolution, a swarm of international war correspondents cornered Mahatma Gandhi.

An aggressive American journalist, accustomed to the brutal armored warfare of World War II, thrust a notebook forward:
"Mr. Gandhi, the British Empire commands battle tanks, Spitfire fighter aircraft, and heavy machine-gun regiments. Japanese armies are at the gates of Burma. You possess not a single rifle or cannon. How in heaven's name do you expect to defeat armed imperial giants with bare hands and spinning wheels? Isn't non-violence simply zero force?"

Gandhi leaned back against his bolster, his toothless grin radiating absolute calm.

"My dear friend, you misunderstand the physics of moral power," Gandhi said gently.

"Military firepower is what I call **plus-force**. When Empire A fires a shell, Empire B must fire a bigger shell. You fight fire with hotter fire, violence with greater violence, until both incinerate each other in ashes. That is the tragedy of Europe today.

"What we practice in India is not zero force; it is **minus-force**! 

"Consider this: An empire does not rule three hundred million people through physical bayonets alone; it rules because millions of Indians carry their files, clean their offices, cook their meals, drive their trains, and obey their laws. 

"Now, when we apply minus-force—when every postal clerk drops his pen, every train driver steps off the engine, every farmer withholds revenue, and every citizen looks the magistrate in the eye and refuses to obey—the colossal imperial machine simply runs out of human grease! A tank cannot plow a field; a bayonet cannot collect taxes. When the people withdraw their consent, the empire collapses under its own hollow weight without our firing a single shot!"

The foreign correspondents scribbled furiously. What they had dismissed as passive weakness was unveiled as the most sophisticated form of asymmetrical mass resistance in modern political philosophy.
